CHICAGO — As Operations Manager, Event Performance Group at Forge, Lombardo is a trusted leader, problem solver and contributor to team development and operational excellence.
p
At Trade Show Executive’s (TSE) Gold 100 Awards & Summit, she was recognized as a 2026 TSE Woman to Watch.
p

Lombardo sat down with TSE for a wide-ranging conversation about her best practices for career advancement, reducing costs while maintaining exceptional event quality and the next big thing in events.
p
ANDREW: Can you tell us how you landed in the trade show industry and what has kept you here?
p

ALEXANDRA: I was a 2020 college graduate with a passion for bringing people together — at the worst time in history. While working full-time, I was able to secure an unpaid event planner position at a non-profit planning their annual gala — virtually.
p

With that experience I was able to find a full-time position at a start-up company planning their events and a few months later landed my position at Questex (now Forge). There is a unique sense of accomplishment that comes from seeing an event come together after months of planning, problem-solving and collaboration.
p
The fast pace keeps me engaged, and the people I’ve met throughout the industry have made it a career I genuinely enjoy.
p
ANDREW: What are some of the skills that have helped you move up in your organization, and how do you refine those skills?
p
ALEXANDRA: Being able to adapt quickly to new software, new processes and different team dynamics and industries is key and has helped me grow my career at Forge.
p
Accepting feedback from others, whether it be good or bad, has helped refine my skills. Also being able to identify what needs to be improved upon for future events has helped as well.
p
ANDREW: How have you helped Forge reduce costs while maintaining exceptional event quality?
p
ALEXANDRA: I have found the key to reducing costs while maintaining exceptional event quality is staying loyal to vendors and developing positive relationships!
p
I view the vendors we work with as friends. I will do whatever it takes to help them and we typically get the same treatment back, especially when it comes to costs.
p
ANDREW: Why is mentorship a key priority for you?
p
ALEXANDRA: I’ve been fortunate to have people throughout my career who have shared their knowledge, trusted me with opportunities and encouraged me to take on challenges that helped me grow.
p
This has been a critical component of my career and I want to be able to do the same for others in the future.
p

Mentorship doesn’t always have to be formal. Sometimes it’s answering a question, sharing something you’ve learned the hard way, making an introduction or simply being someone who will advocate for another person when they’re not in the room.
p
ANDREW: Could you describe an instance of you contributing to an event’s operational excellence and what you accomplished/what challenges you worked through?
p
ALEXANDRA: One of the things I’m most proud of is the amount of operational responsibility I’ve been able to take on for large, complex events.
p
My role often involves managing everything from site selection and space allocation to housing, food and beverage, AV, branding, sponsor activations, managing speakers and onsite execution.
p
I believe in preparing for all circumstances; it’s the overthinker in me.
p
ANDREW: What is your motivation to continue striving for excellence in your work?
p
ALEXANDRA: I enjoy being the person my colleagues, vendors and partners can rely on when something needs to get done.
p
Knowing that I am a trusted resource, even when things get complicated, is a huge motivator.
p
ANDREW: How do you maintain a healthy work-life balance to avoid burnout? How do you encourage others to do the same?
p
ALEXANDRA: Events can make work-life balance challenging because there are periods of intense preparation and onsite execution.
p
I’ve learned that balance isn’t necessarily about having the exact same schedule every week — it’s about recognizing when you’ve been operating at full speed and making time to reset.
p
During slow periods, I encourage my colleagues to shut off notifications and take time to do the things you love.
p
Related. Meet the 2026 TSE Women to Watch: Nataly Laro
p
ANDREW: How do you think women can support each other more in this industry? Or, in what ways do you think the trade show industry is evolving to better support women in leadership roles?
p
ALEXANDRA: Our industry is women-dominated and being supportive of one another is a requirement of the job.
p
It is important to create opportunity for the women just beginning their careers. And to also celebrate all of our successes without viewing them as competitive.
p
I believe strongly that helping someone else succeed does not diminish your own success, but helps you grow as a leader.
p
ANDREW: What do you think the next big thing in the events space is going to be, whether it be related to technology, work models, experiences, etc.?
p
ALEXANDRA: With the introduction of AI and new technologies, I think that there will be more of a shift toward more intentional, personalized, human experiences.
p
Technology and AI have become so good at fooling us from a remote setting, that people will need events and in person networking to have a proper distinction of what is real and what is not.
p

I also think with the current age of social media — organizers are going to become more challenged to think outside of the box to give attendees something they have not experienced before. Something that is “social media worthy.”
p
ANDREW: What strategies have you found most effective for building a strong professional network within the trade show community?
p
ALEXANDRA: Some of the strongest professional relationships I’ve built started from working alongside someone onsite, solving a problem together or simply having a conversation between meetings.
p

The trade show industry is relatively small, and you never know when you’ll work with someone again. I’ve found that being reliable, collaborative and easy to work with is one of the best networking strategies.
p
ANDREW: How do you stay updated on industry trends and changes, and what resources do you recommend to your peers?
p
ALEXANDRA: The best way to stay up to date on industry trends and changes is to go to industry events. It gives me inspiration and prompts new ideas.
p
It’s also a great way to meet people and vendors.
p
I stay current following events on LinkedIn and other social media platforms to see what other people are doing and what is trending.
p
ANDREW: Is there anything else that you would like to add?
p
ALEXANDRA: I’m incredibly grateful for the opportunities I’ve had to grow within this industry and at Forge.
p
When I started in operations, I don’t think I could have predicted how much responsibility, experience and confidence I would gain along the way.
p
I’m proud of the events I’ve helped produce, but I’m equally proud of the people I’ve been able to learn from and work alongside.
p
Being recognized as a Woman to Watch is especially meaningful for me because I hope to continue growing as a leader, while also creating opportunities for the people coming up behind me.
p
